title: Reroute probe capture - scratchbook
content:
Context:
Quick capture of ad-hoc probing session while debugging a user report: high tail latency + intermittent 502s during cross-region handoffs (primarily eu-west1 -> us-central1). This is my personal lab notes — messy, chronological. Keep as a single frame of reference for follow-ups.

Observed symptom (summary):
- ~2:15–2:47 UTC spikes in p95/p99 for routed requests that needed regional failover.
- Some requests returned 502 with code path 'router:handoff-eject'.
- Host-level logs showed sudden increase in route-eject events and subsequent increase in routing-controller restarts.
- Users hit degraded response times when their requests were routed to fallback model variants in another region.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Policy election race where multiple route candidates flagged as degraded simultaneously leading to frequent handoff churn.
2) KV cache TTL mis-alignment causing stale route fingerprints and sudden mismatch with capacity table -> transient 502s.
3) Health-check cascade: a transient downstream timeout causes controller to mark node unhealthy, but autoscaler/prober state lags leading to flapping.
4) Circuit-breaker/backoff miscalculation (incorrect time-base units) that forces route ejects for too-long duration.

What I ran (commands + why):
- kubectl get pods -n routing --selector=app=routing-controller -o wide  # sanity: pod restarts, node
- kubectl logs -n routing routing-controller-5f9b -c controller --since=30m | egrep "handoff|eject|election|ttl|cache"
  # pulled the eject stack and policy election traces

Snippet grabbed (raw):
[2026-03-09T02:17:12.984Z] INFO router:handoff-eject key=usr-47cb, reason=capacity_mismatch, candidates=3, elected=us-central1, ttl_ms=120000
[2026-03-09T02:17:13.012Z] WARN controller:election conflict id=0x9b3e, prev=eu-west1 -> proposed=us-central1, ctx=route-check
[2026-03-09T02:17:13.014Z] ERROR cache:kv HGET routing:fingerprint:usr-47cb -> nil (expected 1)
[2026-03-09T02:17:13.017Z] INFO probe:health-check-retry backend=eu-west1/model-32 status=timeout duration_ms=3010

Interpretation of snippet:
- controller logs show a conflict between an existing election and a proposed one (contention).
- cache returned nil for key that should be present -> suggests either eviction or write-path failure.
- health-check timeout threshold is 3s and we saw a 3010ms result -> triggered dependent logic.

Other useful commands (to reproduce state locally / test):
- redis-cli -h redis-route-prod -p 6379 HGET routing:fingerprint:usr-47cb  # check cached fingerprint
- redis-cli -h redis-route-prod -p 6379 TTL routing:fingerprint:usr-47cb
- kubectl exec -n routing routing-controller-5f9b -- /bin/sh -c 'journalctl -u routing-controller -n 200 | egrep "election|handoff|ttl|cache"'
- curl -i -X POST https://routing-api.internal/v1/eval --data '{"user_id":"usr-47cb","region":"eu-west1"}' | jq .  # simulate decision path
- tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/reroute-capture.pcap 'host 10.1.4.22 and port 6379'  # capture Redis ops around failure window

Quick local repro attempt (notes):
- Replayed probe with routing-api POST -> got 'fallback:us-central1' in 4/5 runs.
- On one run got 502 with body: {"error":"route_eject","code":"HANDOFF_EJECT","meta":"no-fingerprint"}

Error payloads seen in logs (collected):
{"ts":"2026-03-09T02:17:13.019Z","err":"HANDOFF_EJECT","user":"usr-47cb","phase":"decide","detail":"kv-miss and health-timeout"}
{"ts":"2026-03-09T02:19:01.221Z","err":"ROUTE_FLAP","user":"usr-12a5","phase":"election","detail":"conflict-waiting"}

Things that did NOT change recently (from infra config):
- Redis cluster topology unchanged (no maintenance scheduled).
- Routing-controller image last rolled 2026-02-18.
- Autoscaler policy for eu-west1 unchanged.

Interesting correlates (metrics + spans):
- Spike in redis command latency from 40ms to 450ms for ~3 minutes correlates with eject window. (dl: metrics/redis.latency.p99)
- Traces show a single request sometimes doing: route-check -> kv-get -> health-check (timeout) -> fallback eval -> route-eject.

Mini root-cause note (work-in-progress):
- Leading theory: transient congestive latency on redis (maybe transient network blip between routing controller pods and redis replicas) caused HGET to return nil or timed out. Controller treated cache-miss as 'unknown state' so it evals health-checks; since health-checks hit the 3s threshold at same time, multiple controllers concurrently proposed new elections -> conflict -> some flows ended up ejecting while others accepted. The conflict log + 'nil' cache seems consistent.

Short-term mitigation ideas (quick & reversible):
- Increase redis client timeout in routing-controller (-> from 200ms to 500ms) behind a feature flag to reduce false nulls. Risk: longer request path blocking.
- Push a conservative TTL increase on fingerprint keys to reduce eviction-triggered nils.
- Temporarily route around eu-west1 for lower-priority traffic while we investigate (rate-limited fallback).

Longer-term fixes to explore:
- Add jittered backoff to election attempts to reduce simultaneous competing elections.
- Make controller treat kv-miss as 'degraded-read' and preferentially consult latest election leader before ejecting.
- Improve redis client resiliency (connection pooling, prefer local read replica when available).

Next steps I will take (owners):
- Evan: attach tcpdump capture for 02:15-02:20 window and upload to /tmp on infra-probe host. (TODO)
- Maya: reproduce redis latency spike in staging by simulating saturation on redis-replica-2. (TODO)
- Carlos: instrument controller to emit metric routing.election.concurrent_attempts and a histogram of kv-miss durations. (TODO)

Notes/commands to run later (for follow-up):
- run 'redis-benchmark -t get -h redis-route-prod -c 50 -n 100000' from eu-west1-forwarder-host to approximate client contention.
- run 'strace -tt -p <routing-controller-pid> -f -e trace=network' for short window to look at socket timeouts (careful on prod).
- add 'election_attempt_id' in logs to correlate multi-controller attempts.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the redis latency pattern limited to routing-controller clients or global? (need redis slowlog + proxy metrics)
- Why did health-checks cluster at exactly the same ~3s threshold? Is there a clock skew or scheduling quirk causing probe batching?

Random scratch ideas (might be dumb but worth capturing):
- Could we opportunistically cache a fallback-leader pointer (small sentinel key) that controllers consult before electing? Saves round-trips.
- Add a short (250ms) probabilistic sleep before trying to re-elect when conflict count > 0 (cheap jitter)

Conclusion:
- Current short-term priority: capture packet-level evidence & reproduce redis latency in staging. If reproduced, aim for a conservative client-timeout bump and TTL tweak behind flags while we implement jittered/election-smearing logic.

-- Evan
